title: Joint 2018-2026 TESS fits do not require a tilted or eccentric orbit for the WASP-105 candidate
abstract: We test the geometry of the unconfirmed 2.0028-day candidate near WASP-105 b with a new joint fit of 87 small-candidate transits and 20 giant-planet transits in nine TESS sectors. Both objects share a free stellar density and a physical quadratic intensity law. A circular model with both orbits in the same plane is only about 1.0 in chi-square above tested fits with one added geometry parameter. A circular fit with a free small impact parameter has a least possible tilt near 3.16 degrees, but the fit gain does not establish a positive tilt. A coplanar candidate with eccentricity near 0.12 at a fixed periapse angle gives a similar fit. Native-time model checks support the size of this small difference. We preserve profile fits, sector-noise simulations, dilution tests and sector deletion tests. This is a new use of the existing observations, not an independent observing confirmation. The result gives no reliable transit-loss date, unique host, eccentricity detection or migration history. External light curves stay outside the baseline package. Code checks source hashes and regenerates the evidence in separate scratch.

display.caption: Shared-star geometry test. Local impact-parameter profile, model-only transit curves, and sector-noise simulation gains. The circular coplanar state is within about 1.0 chi-square of tested alternatives.
